sections.normalized_html:
We are given that [MATH: y = p(x) + 9,] so to find the values of [MATH: p(x),] we subtract [MATH: 9] from each [MATH: y]-value:

[MATH: p(− 8)|= 6 − 9 = − 3; p(− 5)|= − 3 − 9 = − 12; p(− 2)|= 6 − 9 = − 3]

Now, we observe that [MATH: p(-8) = p(-2) = -3.] Since these values are equal and symmetric, the axis of symmetry must lie halfway between [MATH: x = -8] and [MATH: x = -2.] Hence, the axis of symmetry is

[MATH: x = \dfrac{-8 + (-2)}{2} = -5.]

So, the vertex occurs at [MATH: x = -5,] and since [MATH: p(-5) = -12,] the vertex is the point [MATH: (-5,-12).]

Thus, the equation of the parabola in vertex form is given by the following equation:

[MATH: p(x) = a(x+5)^2 - 12]

We can compute [MATH: a] by substituting any of the obtained function values into the equation above. Let's take the value [MATH: p(-8)=-3{:}]

[MATH: p(x)|= a(x + 5)^{2} − 12; − 3|= a(− 8 + 5)^{2} − 12; − 3|= a(− 3)^{2} − 12; − 3|= 9a − 12; 9a|= 9; a|= 1]

So, the equation of the parabola [MATH: y=p(x)] is

[MATH: p(x) = (x+5)^2 - 12.]

To find the [MATH: y]-intercept of the graph of [MATH: y = p(x),] we need to compute [MATH: p(0){:}]

[MATH: p(0)|= (0 + 5)^{2} − 12; = 25 − 12; = 13]

So, the [MATH: y]-intercept is [MATH: \bbox[3pt,border:1px solid lightgray]{13}.]

sections.normalized_html:
We are told that [MATH: g] is a quadratic function, so the relationship between [MATH: x] and [MATH: g] must have the form [MATH: g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c.]

We will use the values from the table to write a system of equations for the parameters [MATH: a,] [MATH: b,] and [MATH: c.]

  • From [MATH: x = -2,] we have [MATH: g(− 2)|= 0; a(− 2)^{2} + b(− 2) + c|= 0; 4a − 2b + c|= 0.]

  • From [MATH: x = 1,] we have [MATH: g(1)|= − 3; a(1)^{2} + b(1) + c|= − 3; a + b + c|= − 3.]

  • From [MATH: x = 0,] we have [MATH: g(0)|= 2; a(0)^{2} + b(0) + c|= 2; c|= 2.]

Now, we substitute [MATH: c = 2] into the other two equations.

  • From [MATH: 4a - 2b + c = 0,] we have [MATH: 4a − 2b + 2|= 0; 4a − 2b|= − 2; 2a − b|= − 1.]

  • From [MATH: a + b + c = -3,] we have [MATH: a + b + 2|= − 3; a + b|= − 5.]

So, we get the following system of equations: [MATH: 2a − b|= − 1; a + b|= − 5]

Adding the two equations gives [MATH: 3a|= − 6; a|= − 2.]

Now, we substitute the value [MATH: a=-2] into [MATH: a + b = -5{:}] [MATH: -2 + b = -5\quad\Rightarrow\quad b = -3]

Finally, collecting [MATH: a=-2,] [MATH: b=-3,] and [MATH: c=2,] we get [MATH: g(x)|= ax^{2} + bx + c; = − 2x^{2} − 3x + 2.]

EXPLANATION

[MATH: p(− 8)|= 6 − 9 = − 3; p(− 5)|= − 3 − 9 = − 12; p(− 2)|= 6 − 9 = − 3]

[MATH: p(x) = a(x+5)^2 - 12]
